headword: {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}

definitions.explanation: Parking a vehicle in a location or manner that violates traffic laws. A common urban issue in Japan where street parking is heavily regulated.

examples.japanese: {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}で{罰金|ばっきん}を{取|と}られた。
examples.english: I was fined for illegal parking.

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りは{違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There is a lot of illegal parking on this street.

examples.japanese: {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}の{取|と}り{締|し}まりが{厳|きび}しくなったおかげで、{道路|どうろ}が{広|ひろ}く{使|つか}えるようになった。
examples.english: Thanks to stricter enforcement against illegal parking, the roads have become easier to use.

notes:
Composed of {違法|いほう} (illegal, unlawful) and {駐車|ちゅうしゃ} (parking). In Japan, street parking regulations are strict, and since 2006, private enforcement officers ({駐車監視員|ちゅうしゃかんしいん}) have been deployed to issue tickets for illegal parking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}の{取|と}り{締|し}まり: crackdown on illegal parking
- {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}{禁止|きんし}: no illegal parking (on signs)
- {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}で{罰金|ばっきん}: fined for illegal parking
- {違法駐車|いほうちゅうしゃ}を{通報|つうほう}する: to report illegal parking

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {路上駐車|ろじょうちゅうしゃ}: street parking — parking on the road (may or may not be illegal)
- {駐車違反|ちゅうしゃいはん}: parking violation — essentially the same meaning, more commonly heard in everyday speech
- {迷惑駐車|めいわくちゅうしゃ}: nuisance parking — parking that causes inconvenience, not necessarily illegal
